summary:
Roraima stands under Brazil's national framework rather than a state statute of its own: the provisions on same-sex marriage, adoption, gender-marker recognition, anti-discrimination and custody placement described in the national record apply in Boa Vista and across the state without local modification, and the full national layer is carried by the parent record.

Two Roraima instruments are specific to this state. On 9 August 2023 a measure published in the Official Gazette of Boa Vista, approved by Mayor Genilson Costa of the Solidarity party, prohibited transgender athletes from competing in sport according to their gender identity. The measure is municipal and confined to athletics; it does not alter criminal law, document rules or entry conditions for a visitor.

Roraima State Ordinance No. 1,797/2023 is a state-level instrument directed at combating homophobia, placing the state government on the record in favour of protection rather than restriction.

No region-specific incidents of violence, police conduct, healthcare access disputes or detention-placement problems for trans people in Roraima were identified in the source inventory; the national assessment carries the risk picture for this state.
tangentialFactors:
An OAB/SP guide for expatriates observes that legal protections are broadly enforced in Brazil's major urban centres, while smaller cities and rural areas may present more social friction despite identical legal rights. Boa Vista is a small-state capital without the established LGBTQ legal infrastructure of São Paulo or Rio de Janeiro, so a visitor should expect fewer practical resources behind the same formal guarantees.

OutRight International reports that Brazil's legal advances for sexual and gender minorities face repeal pressure in a conservative Congress, and that the country retains one of the world's highest rates of violence against such minorities, trans people in particular. That pressure is national in origin but is felt through local instruments such as the 2023 Boa Vista measure.
localsOnly:
Roraima State Ordinance No. 1,797/2023 is the state's own anti-homophobia instrument and is the resident-facing protection created at this level of government.

Trans athletes living in Boa Vista fall under the 9 August 2023 municipal prohibition on competing according to gender identity. The source inventory does not say whether the measure reaches school sport, private clubs or public facilities, and does not record any challenge to it.

Gender-marker change by self-declaration, without surgery, hormones or professional evaluation, is available to Roraima residents through the national procedure; the inventory records no state-level impediment or additional requirement imposed in this state.
outOfScopeNotes:
Unresolved: the inventory does not state whether the 9 August 2023 Boa Vista measure has been litigated, amended or repealed, nor which sporting bodies it binds.

Unresolved: no enforcement data for Roraima State Ordinance No. 1,797/2023 is sourced, so its practical effect on complaints and prosecutions is unknown.

Not sourced: the inventory contains no Roraima figures for anti-trans violence, no account of police handling of complaints, no information on access to gender-affirming care through state facilities, and no information on placement of trans detainees in the state.

Not sourced: whether Roraima's courts have applied the national hate-crime provisions in any recorded case.
